title: Conditional Access: which sign-ins does Microsoft Entra allow, and what must users do first?
summary: The page needs one factual correction: an application can encounter Conditional Access through the services it calls even when no policy directly targets that application. The documented licensing, limits and eight governance control surfaces otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Policy creation and assignment configuration are at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies. ... Select New policy. ... Under Access controls > Grant, select Block access.
claims.fix: Extend this row's UI path to 'Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Access controls > Grant > Block access', which the cited page documents and the row's note already gives.

claims.claim: Conditional Access is Microsoft Entra's policy engine for access decisions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access brings signals together, to make decisions, and enforce organizational policies. Conditional Access is Microsoft's Zero Trust policy engine

claims.claim: Policies are if-then statements requiring an action to access a resource.
claims.quote: Conditional Access policies at their simplest are if-then statements: if a user wants to access a resource, then they must complete an action.

claims.claim: Policy enforcement follows completion of first-factor authentication.
claims.quote: Conditional Access policies are enforced after first-factor authentication is completed.

claims.claim: Conditional Access is not a frontline defence against denial-of-service attacks.
claims.quote: Conditional Access isn't intended to be an organization's frontline defense for scenarios like denial-of-service (DoS) attacks

claims.claim: Conditional Access can use signals from such attacks to decide access.
claims.quote: but it can use signals from these events to determine access.

claims.claim: An app that no policy targets gets no Conditional Access decision.
claims.quote: the policy isn't set directly on a client (public/native) application, but is applied when a client calls a service. For example, a policy set on SharePoint service applies to all clients calling SharePoint.
claims.fix: Replace 'an app that no policy targets gets no Conditional Access decision' with 'Conditional Access applies to the resources an app requests, so an app can encounter a policy even when it is not directly targeted'. The cited Target resources page explicitly documents this distinction.
